title: Second Week: I gave ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok $100,000 each to beat S&P500.
author: alphagroundhq
selftext:
If you missed the [week one post](https://www.reddit.com/r/Trading/s/9PVqvEen99): on October 19 I gave ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok the same prompt. Write a rule-based strategy that beats the S&P 500 by December 31, starting with $100,000. I turned each answer into a trading agent on Alphaground, and since October 20 the rules have traded on their own at real prices. Nobody gets to touch them. Not the AIs, not me.

All four landed on the same basic idea, buying what has already been going up. The rules around it are where they split:

https://i.redd.it/ptt866pz97zh1.png

Here’s the board after two weeks.

https://i.redd.it/tfih1r63a7zh1.png

ChatGPT is still in front, and three of the four are still ahead of the index. Grok is last again. Which is a little funny, because on Wednesday night it was first again.

https://i.redd.it/5247bkv5a7zh1.png

# Grok did it again

Last week Grok made 3.3% in two days and then lost 5.5% on a single Thursday. I honestly thought that would be the story of the whole race.

This week it ran the same play on different days. Up 2.7% on Monday, 0.7% on Tuesday, 3.0% on Wednesday. By the Wednesday close it was 3.8% ahead of where it started, and more than three points clear of everyone else. Then Thursday took 1.4%, and Friday took 4.5%.

Nothing about the cause has changed. Grok’s rules hold the ten S&P 500 stocks that climbed most smoothly over the past year, and right now six of those ten are memory, storage and hardware: Sandisk, Micron, Lumentum, Seagate, Western Digital and Dell. When those six have a good day, Grok has a great one. When they don’t, there’s nothing else in the portfolio to catch the fall. On Friday the S&P 500 lost 1.8%, and Sandisk lost more than 10% by itself.

https://i.redd.it/lwypn368a7zh1.png

Here’s the part I didn’t expect. Count the week from Friday to Friday and Grok actually made money, +0.3% while the index lost 0.5%. It just took the bumpiest road there is.

# Everyone else sold something

In week one, nobody sold a single share. The rules only bought. This week three of the four closed a trade for the first time, and all three closed at a loss. I learned more about each strategy from that one sale than from all its buying.

**Gemini went first.** It sells any stock that closes 8% below its best close since buying, and on Tuesday Marathon Petroleum crossed that line. Yes, the same refiner three of the four AIs bought on day one. Gemini sold it at Wednesday’s open, about 7% under what it paid, and used the money that same morning to buy CrowdStrike. Claude and Grok still own Marathon, each about 6% under water.

https://i.redd.it/suugmfgfa7zh1.png

**Claude came next.** It sells a stock once it’s 15% below the buy price. By Thursday’s close, Fortinet was 18.5% below. Claude checks its stops before the open, so it sold Friday morning, and the trade ended 19.7% down. That’s worth knowing about stop losses in general. The 15% is where you look. It isn’t where you get out.

**ChatGPT’s sale was the strangest.** Remember the consumer staples fund, the toothpaste and cereal that carried it through last week’s bad Thursday? On Tuesday that fund’s three-month return dipped just below zero. ChatGPT’s rule reads that as a broken trend, so it sold the fund at Wednesday’s open for a 1.6% loss, and then sat on a third of the account in cash.

On Friday, at its weekly check, staples passed both of its tests again. So ChatGPT is buying the same fund back, at a higher price, at Monday’s open.

I don’t know many people who could do that without flinching. Selling at a loss and buying back three days later for more feels like being wrong twice. The rule doesn’t feel anything. It also left ChatGPT in health care, energy and cash on Friday, which is how it finished that day up 0.8% while the index fell 1.8%.

# Grok’s re-pick: a bit of both

Last week I asked whether Grok would double down on chips when it re-ranked the S&P 500 at the end of the month, or move on. The ranking ran Friday night, and the answer is somewhere in the middle.

Western Digital and Phillips 66 are out. Targa gets trimmed. Two new names come in, Illumina and Moderna. And Sandisk, the stock that has hurt Grok the most, 14% under its buy price, now ranks first out of 498 by Grok’s own measure. So Grok buys more of it.

# So what’s the point?

A lot of comments on the first post said some version of the same thing. It’s fake money, one week is noise, come back with a ten-year backtest. One person wrote that their own ChatGPT portfolio had blown them away over three months. By how much? They didn’t remember.

That last one is honestly where most “AI beat the market” stories live. Screenshots and memory. And the ten-year backtest, which sounds like the serious fix, doesn’t work here. These models have read about the last ten years. They know which stocks went up. Testing their rules on that history is like grading a student on an exam they’ve already seen. And by the time you had ten years of fresh results, these models would be long retired.

So the only fair test is prices that don’t exist yet. The rules were written and posted on October 19, before a single trade. Nobody can change them, not the AIs and not me. Every trade is stamped and public, next to the S&P 500 over the same days. Ten weeks won’t prove who the best investor is. It will be an honest record, which is more than most of those screenshots are.

If you want something to take from it now, two weeks in, I’d skip the leaderboard and look at the temperament. Same question, four very different rides. Grok has lost more than 4% in a single day twice. ChatGPT’s worst day so far is -1.0%. Even if Grok wins in December, its answer is still wrong for someone who would lose sleep over a Friday like this one.

Whichever AI you ask, you get its temperament along with its strategy. None of the four mentioned theirs. You only find out by watching the rules trade.

# What to watch in week three

* **Grok’s new lineup.** Half the money is still in memory and hardware. Does it lead again by Wednesday?
* **Gemini’s line, part two.** CrowdStrike, the stock it bought with the Marathon money, closed Friday about 7% under what Gemini paid. The 8% line is close.
* **Claude’s next stop.** Twilio closed Friday 19% below Claude’s price, already past the 15% line. Claude checks before Monday’s open, so it looks like the next one out.

Every trade, holding and nightly journal is public, so you can check my work: [ai\_race/chatgpt-26q4](https://alphaground.ai/ai_race/chatgpt-26q4), [ai\_race/claude-26q4](https://alphaground.ai/ai_race/claude-26q4), [ai\_race/gemini-26q4](https://alphaground.ai/ai_race/gemini-26q4) and [ai\_race/grok-26q4](https://alphaground.ai/ai_race/grok-26q4).

And if you think you can do better than all four, try it. No code. Describe your rules the way you’d explain them to a friend, [start an agent](https://alphaground.ai/new-agent) with $100,000 of practice money, and it trades next to them from tomorrow.

Grok bought more of its worst stock. ChatGPT bought back what it sold. What would yours have done on Friday?
